front_blocks.md: Define **ionic bond**.

back_blocks.md: An **ionic bond** is the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions, formed when electrons are transferred from a metal atom (forming a cation) to a non-metal atom (forming an anion).

cards.back_md: An **ionic bond** is the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions, formed when electrons are transferred from a metal atom (forming a cation) to a non-metal atom (forming an anion).

front_blocks.md: What electronic configuration do ions typically adopt after ionic bond formation?

back_blocks.md: Ions adopt the electronic configuration of the nearest **noble gas**, giving them a full outer shell. For example, K<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup> both have the configuration [2,8,8], the same as argon.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
In ionic bonding, the metal atom gains electrons to form a cation.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The **metal atom loses** electrons to form a positively charged cation. The non-metal atom gains electrons to form a negatively charged anion.

front_blocks.md: Ionic compounds form a **..........**  structure in which cations and anions are arranged in a regular repeating pattern so the overall compound is electrically **..........**  .

back_blocks.md: Ionic compounds form a **lattice** structure in which cations and anions are arranged in a regular repeating pattern so the overall compound is electrically **neutral**.

cards.back_md: Ionic compounds form a **lattice** structure in which cations and anions are arranged in a regular repeating pattern so the overall compound is electrically **neutral**.

front_blocks.md: Define **anion**.

back_blocks.md: An **anion** is a negatively charged ion formed when a non-metal atom **gains** one or more electrons during ionic bond formation.

cards.back_md: An **anion** is a negatively charged ion formed when a non-metal atom **gains** one or more electrons during ionic bond formation.

front_blocks.md: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?

back_blocks.md: The **electrostatic attractions** between oppositely charged ions in the lattice act in all directions and are very strong. A large amount of energy is needed to overcome these forces, resulting in high melting points.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The ionic bond acts only between two specific oppositely charged ions.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The ionic bond acts in **all directions**. Each ion is attracted to all surrounding oppositely charged ions in the lattice.

front_blocks.md: In potassium chloride, the potassium atom **..........**  one electron to form a **..........**  ion, and the chlorine atom **..........**  that electron to form a chloride ion.

back_blocks.md: In potassium chloride, the potassium atom **loses** one electron to form a **K**<sup>**+**</sup> ion, and the chlorine atom **gains** that electron to form a chloride ion.

front_blocks.md: How can you use the periodic table to predict the charge on an ion formed by ionic bonding?

back_blocks.md: The **group number** indicates how many electrons a metal loses (for Groups 1 and 2) or how many a non-metal gains (for Groups 6 and 7), giving the ion charge. For example, Group 2 metals lose 2 electrons to form 2+ cations.

front_blocks.md: What ions are formed when sodium and chlorine react, and what is the formula of the ionic compound produced?

back_blocks.md: Sodium loses 1 electron to form Na<sup>+</sup> and chlorine gains 1 electron to form Cl<sup>-</sup>. The ionic compound formed is **NaCl** (sodium chloride).

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
In magnesium oxide, magnesium forms a 2+ ion and oxygen forms a 2- ion.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Magnesium (Group 2) loses 2 electrons to form Mg<sup>2+</sup> and oxygen (Group 6) gains 2 electrons to form O<sup>2-</sup>, giving the neutral compound MgO.

front_blocks.md: In calcium fluoride, one Ca<sup>2+</sup> ion bonds with **..........**  F<sup>-</sup> ions because each fluorine can only accept **..........**  electron, giving the formula **..........**  .

back_blocks.md: In calcium fluoride, one Ca<sup>2+</sup> ion bonds with **two** F<sup>-</sup> ions because each fluorine can only accept **one** electron, giving the formula **CaF**<sub>**2**</sub>.

front_blocks.md: Define **dot and cross diagram**.

back_blocks.md: A **dot and cross diagram** is a representation of ionic or covalent bonding in which electrons from different atoms are shown as dots or crosses, indicating which atom each electron originated from.

front_blocks.md: How many lithium ions are needed to form lithium nitride (Li<sub>3</sub>N), and why?

back_blocks.md: **Three** Li<sup>+</sup> ions are needed because nitrogen gains 3 electrons to form N<sup>3-</sup>, and each lithium can only donate 1 electron. Three Li<sup>+</sup> ions balance the 3- charge of one N<sup>3-</sup> ion.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Aluminium oxide has the formula AlO.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

Aluminium forms Al<sup>3+</sup> and oxygen forms O<sup>2-</sup>. To balance the charges, 2 Al<sup>3+</sup> ions and 3 O<sup>2-</sup> ions are needed, giving the formula **Al**<sub>**2**</sub>**O**<sub>**3**</sub>.

back_blocks.md: In ionic bonding, the final ionic solid is always electrically **neutral** because positive and negative charges **cancel** each other.

front_blocks.md: What charge does the ion formed by a Group 7 non-metal carry, and why?

back_blocks.md: A Group 7 non-metal carries a **1- charge** because it needs to gain **1 electron** to achieve a full outer shell (8 electrons), matching the configuration of the nearest noble gas.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
In NaCl, both the Na<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup> ions adopt the electronic configuration of argon.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Na<sup>+</sup> has configuration [2,8] matching **neon**, while Cl<sup>-</sup> has configuration [2,8,8] matching **argon**. They adopt different noble gas configurations, not both argon.
